newsitem.title: UK: UK bank lending posts record rise in Q1 - BBA.
newsitem.headline: UK bank lending posts record rise in Q1 - BBA.

text.p: Lending by major British banking groups rose by a record amount in the first quarter of the year, the British Bankers' Association said on Tuesday.
The BBA said the increase in lending totalled 11.388 billion stg in the three months to the end of March, compared with a revised underlying figure of 6.5 billion for the last quarter of 1996.
"The increase in the major banks' lending in the first quarter was...a record for the MBBG series by some margin," said BBA director-general Tim Sweeney.
Lending to persons, up 1.9 percent by 3.568 billion stg, accounted for a little over 50 percent of the total.
Lending to industrial and commercial companies was basically unchanged, having risen sharply in three of the previous four quarters.
Mortgage lending rose by 2.339 billion stg, up 1.6 percent on the previous quarter while consumer credit jumped by 1.251 billion stg or three percent.
"Mortgage lending strengthened significantly from the previous quarter, while consumer credit maintained the increased momentum evident since the end of 1995," Sweeney said.

Borrowing by manufacturing industry fell by 404 million pounds,with substantial falls for food, drink and tobacco companies. The hotels and catering sector, property companies, other retail distribution and motor retailing all borrowed less.
But financial services, the chemical industry and oil and gas extractors saw lending increase.

"Borrowing by industry and commerce was virtually flat," Sweeney said. "There was, however, very substantial credit demand from companies in the financial sector, met in part through considerable use of repo facilities," Sweeney Said.
Lending by was of reverse repos rose by about 2.9 billion stg in the first quarter, largely due to activity in March.
